# master_backup

[← Command index](README.md)

Back up the local locker to one or more remote lockers in one unattended run.

## Synopsis

```
master_backup [options]
```

## Description

Treats the source locker (normally `Local`) as the authoritative copy and pushes new
and changed files to each destination locker, by default `Hetzner` and `Gdrive`. It
asks for one confirmation and then runs without prompting. It is additive by default:
files that exist only on a destination are kept unless `--recycle_orphans` is given.

For each destination it:

1. Builds an MD5 hash map of the source and of the destination and compares them by
   relative path. Local lockers are hashed on disk; remotes are listed with
   `rclone lsjson --hash`, and SFTP remotes such as Hetzner are read from their
   `.locker_hashes.db` sidecar instead.
2. Uploads files missing from the destination or whose hash differs. Plain files go up
   in one `rclone copy --files-from`. For a destination marked `encrypted` in its
   locker settings, files are encrypted into a staging tree in the cache directory and
   uploaded in batches of about 4 GiB.
3. Refreshes the destination's hash sidecar from the local content, once, when the
   source is a local locker and the destination is an SFTP remote.

Each destination's configured `excluded_dirs` are left out of both the comparison and
the upload. This is the unattended form of `locker_sync_tool`.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-l, --local_locker <local_locker>` | Locker to back up from; its content is treated as authoritative. Default: `Local`. Allowed: `All`, `Local`, `Hetzner`, `Gdrive`, `External`. |
| `-r, --remote_lockers <remote_lockers>` | Comma-separated locker names to back up to; unknown names are skipped with a warning. Default: `Hetzner,Gdrive`. |
| `--no_rebuild_sidecars` | Do not refresh the SFTP destinations' hash sidecars after uploading. |
| `--recycle_orphans` | Move destination files that are missing from the source into the destination's `.recycle_bin`; by default they are kept. |
| `--skip_cache` | Rebuild every hash map instead of reusing one cached within the last 24 hours. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Back up the local locker to Hetzner and Gdrive

```bash
master_backup
```

### Show what would be uploaded without uploading anything

```bash
master_backup -p -v
```

### Back up to Hetzner only

```bash
master_backup -r Hetzner
```

### Also move remote files that no longer exist locally into the recycle bin

```bash
master_backup --recycle_orphans
```

### Rehash everything instead of using the cached hash maps

```bash
master_backup --skip_cache
```

## Notes

- Hash maps are cached per locker for 24 hours, including the source's. Files changed locally since the cached map was built are not seen until it expires, so use `--skip_cache` after recent changes.
- A pretend run still hashes local lockers and writes their cache, so the real run that follows can reuse it.
- `--recycle_orphans` moves orphans into the destination's `.recycle_bin`; nothing is hard-deleted. The recycle bin itself is never compared.
- The sidecar refresh is skipped for a destination when any of its uploads failed, so the next run finds and retries the missing files.
- The Hetzner rclone remote needs `disable_hashcheck = true`, since SFTP cannot run `md5sum` to verify transfers; the rclone config JoyBox generates sets it.
